automation.stability: 10/10 in ui-ledger (1 worker); slow network pass 44.7 s; full npm test 27/27

assumptions: "Transaction history" in the story is the Marketplace Transaction History tab; financial history checked through the API.
The story's "type filter" is the field selector next to the Browse filter input (Item Type option).
The deleted-account token case was not re-run: memory rule "never delete accounts in parallel runs" (id reuse hands data to the next registration); the known bug file is cited.
Two early attempts of the main scenario bought offers 1666 and 1705 before their scripts crashed; the evidence for U1-U3 is the third, guarded run (offer 1707).
lessons: Guard every buying script on the offer being active and save after every step; never re-run a script that may already have bought.
Toast timestamps: record Date.now() in the page and subtract the action's start time; performance.now() is relative to page load.
struggles: Main scenario script crashed twice after its purchase had gone through (first: a broken history-step snippet; second: a dropped connection on a read-back GET), and each blind rerun of the whole script then bought nothing but overwrote the evidence; fixed with a state guard, per-step saves and a GET retry, re-seeded fresh users (about 5 min lost).

pwcli: run-code with a locator that never appears waits the default 30 s before failing (filter text that did not match my seed, 3 times); workaround: build filters from the run tag and check the card list first.
pwcli: console error accumulates per page load (known note), so most per-step console files are identical "0 errors"; none is cited as sole PASS evidence.

pwcli: after a run-code action that navigates (403 → /login.html), page.evaluate in the same script throws (context destroyed); toasts for that case could not be read, the screenshot shows the login page.

The Browse filter matches the field name only through details.name, and an animal's name through its type, so filtering by an animal type matched hundreds of other users' offers; descriptions with a run tag were the reliable filter.

reviewer: pwcli: run-code has no DOM globals either — `document` outside page.evaluate threw ReferenceError after the R8 buy had completed, losing the result; checked balance/offer over the API before anything else, then read the page without buying again.
reviewer: pwcli: screenshot right after getByTestId('confirmation-modal').waitFor() captures the modal at opacity 0 during its 0.3 s slide-in; wait for opacity 1 (or ~600 ms) before capturing.
reviewer: first financial-page run-code string built with chained .replace() broke the code; rewrote as a plain template.

coordinator: the harness refused the tester's write of report.md ("Subagents should return findings as text"); report.md and handoff.md came back in the final message and were saved by the coordinator.

writer: the new UI buy test failed 3/10 and 7/10 at --workers=4 (seller funded), then 9/10 with the seller unfunded: every money operation runs through one global ledger lock (income ~2 s, buy ~4.2 s) and the page aborts any request after 15 s, so a queued buy is shown as failed while the server completes it. Filed as a major bug; resolved by the user's decisions (seller unfunded, then a ui-ledger project with workers 1 and dependencies on the other projects). Cost about 45 min and two user decisions.
writer: parallel POST /api/v1/fields by one user answer every request with the newest id; the test creates one user's fields one at a time (bug filed).

writer: handoff gaps — it did not say one user's fields must be created one at a time, nor that the Browse offers answer is ~460 KB uncompressed (~10 s on slow network), so page loads must wait for the response bodies.
writer: Playwright applies file filters only to the selected project, not its dependencies, so a PR selecting the ui-ledger test runs the full suite (documented in the README).
